races.name: Farmhouse Foods Novice Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Radiator Springs
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to this pace setup, Henry De Bromhead 88 days off last run but winning pointer form suggests readiness

runners_data.spotlight: Well held in his two previous handicaps as a jumper but has since won a Cork novice and a staying handicap on the AW; others are a bit more intriguing, however; cheekpieces removed.

runners_data.name: Arslan

runners_data.name: Court Canyon

runners_data.name: Lincoln Du Seuil

runners_data.spotlight: French bumper winner; beaten between 12l and 23l in his maiden hurdles; he's not obviously well in for this first handicap but it's early days and the potential is there to improve; tongue-tie added.

runners_data.name: Withabitofluk

runners_data.name: Camlin Park

runners_data.spotlight: Only 1-6 in points and her 12l maiden hurdle win at Downpatrick (2m2f, good) is very much a standout piece of form over hurdles; others have more pressing claims.

runners_data.name: Wackestone

runners_data.comment: Maiden promise; has to be interest against older opposition on handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Rated 80 on the Flat after three runs; still a maiden after four runs over hurdles but was placed behind respected opposition in the middle two and he has to be interest against older opposition on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Combs
runners_data.note: Consistent placegetter but ordinary last run suggests current form concerns despite Elliott yard

runners_data.spotlight: 1m4f winner; 0-6 as a hurdler but was third off this mark at Christmas and then ran into the smart Proactif here in January; the concern is his ordinary run last time at Down Royal (maiden).

runners_data.spotlight: Won a point 13 months ago; no closer than 12l in four runs under rules but this gelding will probably be seen in a brighter light sooner or later; market needs checking on handicap debut.

runners_data.name: Mart Lane
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with improving form, Barry Connell stable running just 0/2 recently but horse has potential
runners_data.comment: Improved second in a maiden latest and he brings potential off this sort of mark
runners_data.spotlight: Lightly-raced 5yo who raised his game to finish second in a Wexford maiden (soft) and he brings potential off this sort of mark; respected.

runners_data.name: Migdam

runners_data.comment: Good and bad on the Flat since winning a maiden hurdle at Thurles; others preferred
runners_data.spotlight: Only had two runs over hurdles, last time winning a maiden on good ground at Tramore (first-time hood); good and bad on the Flat since then; lacks jumping experience for a race of this nature.

runners_data.name: Hesgonethatway
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse but 9lb rise after Naas win may have stopped momentum

runners_data.spotlight: Perhaps won too well at Naas (soft/heavy) as the 9lb rise was surely a factor in his defeat at Thurles, though he still ran okay in fairness; others are more intriguing here.

runners_data.name: Kentucky Beach

runners_data.spotlight: 0-7; disappointing favourite at Tramore last time but has had a break since then and his previous seconds in 2m handicaps (in a tongue-tie) need respecting; each-way claims with tongue-tie back on.

runners_data.name: Walk On Annilog
runners_data.note: Prominent mare but hasn't shown enough in recent handicaps to suggest mark is workable
runners_data.comment: Hasn't performed badly in either of her handicaps without looking ahead of her mark
runners_data.spotlight: Hasn't performed badly in either of her handicaps without looking ahead of her mark; this is no easier.

runners_data.name: Thankyouforthedays

runners_data.name: Premier Rogue
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but showed little when stepping into handicaps at Leopardstown
runners_data.comment: Some promise in bumpers/maidens but offered little on switch to handicaps at Leopardstown
runners_data.spotlight: Some promise in bumpers/maidens but offered little on switch to handicaps at Leopardstown (14-1).

runners_data.name: Poet's Gale
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but opening handicap mark looks harsh based on poor maiden form
runners_data.comment: Well held in three maiden; opening mark looks plenty high on that evidence

runners_data.name: Desert Haven

runners_data.comment: 0-10 over hurdles and come up shy in less competitive races than this
runners_data.spotlight: Two respectable Flat runs last month but 0-10 over hurdles and has come up shy in less competitive races than this.

races.paceDynamic: Seven confirmed front runners including Arslan, Lincoln Du Seuil, Jet To Monte Carlo, Likealightswitch, Camlin Park, Kentucky Beach and Thankyouforthedays will create a fierce early gallop over this 2m trip on testing ground. With 9 horses wanting prominent positions, severe traffic problems are guaranteed approaching the business end, particularly 2-3 hurdles out where the field will concertina. The relentless pace on soft ground will expose stamina limitations and create a war of attrition. This race shape heavily favours hold-up horses who can avoid the early carnage and pick up the pieces late, with patient riders holding the decisive advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners go too fast early and burn out on the soft ground
scenarios.body: The fierce pace will collapse the leaders in the final half-mile, setting up perfectly for the closers who avoided the early battle. Patient rides on horses like Radiator Springs and Kabylia will be rewarded as they pick off tired leaders.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Survive
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but sustainable with smart tactical rides from the prominent brigade
scenarios.body: Horses like Saveforarainyday and Withabitofluk can position just off the leaders without getting embroiled in the speed duel. They'll have enough left to kick clear when the leaders weaken but before the hold-up horses arrive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Surprise Front Runner
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters gets an easy lead due to others taking each other on
scenarios.body: Thankyouforthedays or Likealightswitch could steal a march if the other leaders neutralise each other early. The winner will need to be tough enough to see out the trip when challenged.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow early due to too many leaders eyeing each other up
scenarios.body: A messy tactical affair could develop with no one wanting to make the running, turning it into a sprint finish. This would suit horses with a turn of foot regardless of usual running style.

watchPoints.text: Massive early pace collision between Arslan, Lincoln Du Seuil, Jet To Monte Carlo, Likealightswitch, Kentucky Beach, Thankyouforthedays and Camlin Park will create chaos
Traffic problems at 3rd last hurdle where 9 prominent runners will hit the bottleneck simultaneously as pace collapses
Radiator Springs and Kabylia positioning - if they get trapped behind walls of horses they cannot win despite suiting the pace
Saveforarainyday's hood removal suggests supreme confidence from Cromwell yard - market will reveal expectations
Michael Kenneally's 5lb claim on Tatateo meaningless if he cannot navigate the traffic problems this race will create

races.name: O'Driscoll's Irish Whiskey Juvenile Hurdle (Grade 2)

runners_data.name: Kai Lung
runners_data.note: Strong front-runner on debut win but 24 days off and needs to prove stamina over this trip on soft ground
runners_data.comment: Maiden win reads well; suffered interference when pulled up in the Triumph
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent Flat horse in France; had the Fred Winter winner Saratoga back in third when winning his maiden at Naas (first-time hood; heavy) and unwise to read too much into his no-show in the Triumph (33-1) as he lost his position after mid-race interference; remains capable of better.

runners_data.name: North Shore
runners_data.note: Classic hold-up horse whose French form suggests stamina reserves, though Triumph effort was disappointing
runners_data.comment: Never gave his true running in the Triumph and can be given another chance in a Grade 2
runners_data.spotlight: 1m4f winner in France; twice beaten about 11l behind the smart Narciso Has and, for whatever reason, he didn't appear to give his true running in the Triumph (16-1); could easily be given another chance back in a Grade 2.

runners_data.name: Macho Man
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who finished strongly behind Proactif last time and represents excellent Mullins tactical nous
runners_data.comment: 12-1 for the Triumph and yet his race ended after a bad mid-race blunder; promising
runners_data.spotlight: Easy winner of his only hurdle run in France; inexperience evident when chasing home Proactif here in January (yielding; finished his race off well); only 12-1 for the Triumph and yet all hopes went west with a bad mid-race blunder after which he was pulled up; remains very promising.

runners_data.name: Moulin Labbe
runners_data.note: Natural leader but 37 days since last run may blunt his early speed in this competitive pace battle
runners_data.comment: 13l winner at Navan; chaser in the making and clearly open to vast improvement
runners_data.spotlight: French bumper winner; weak in the betting when a remote fifth on his hurdle/stable debut but then odds-on when coming home 13l to the good at Navan (2m, heavy); raised in grade here but considered a chaser in the making and clearly open to vast improvement.

runners_data.name: Proactif
runners_data.note: Proven front-runner with tactical speed but Triumph flop raises questions about his temperament under pressure
runners_data.comment: If forgiven his Festival blip in the Triumph then his credentials are clear to see
runners_data.spotlight: Reportedly never travelled when a disappointing favourite in the Triumph; he did beat the Cheltenham winner Apolon De Charnie in France and he looked good when accounting for Macho Man here on his stable debut; if forgiven his Festival blip, then his credentials are clear to see.

runners_data.name: Harwa
runners_data.note: Another pace-setter but trainer Paul Nolan's 0/7 record in last 14 days suggests stable not firing
runners_data.comment: Course maiden winner; looked on a tough mark in the Fred Winter and ran accordingly
runners_data.spotlight: Twice runner-up in France; well on top late on to win his maiden here (heavy) and it was no great surprise to see him struggle in the Fred Winter off what looked a tough opening mark (good to soft; 28-1); others have superior form.

runners_data.name: Majolique
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but mare's allowance helps, though she's proven over similar distances on heavy
runners_data.comment: 1m2f French winner; impressed at Naas when widely expected to need the run
runners_data.spotlight: Beat respected opposition in a 1m2f French race; reportedly surprised her connections in winning so well at Naas (1m7f, heavy) and expected to come on leaps and bounds for that; engaged in a Grade 1 at Aintree next week but runs here; Townend's chosen one.

runners_data.name: Adrienne
runners_data.note: Solid each-way claims with consistent record and trainer Walsh can place them despite poor recent strike-rate

runners_data.name: Michonne
runners_data.note: Improving type whose second last time suggests coming to hand, though yard form remains concerning
runners_data.comment: Second to Majolique at Naas and looks capable of holding her own at this level
runners_data.spotlight: Bought for 185,000euros out of top French Flat yard for whom she won at 1m3f and 2m; well held in a Leopardstown maiden over Christmas but much better when second to Majolique at Naas and looks capable of holding her own at this level.

runners_data.name: Minella Boss
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing tongue-tie for first time, suggesting connections expect improved effort from him
runners_data.comment: Bumped into useful opposition before winning his maiden on heavy ground at Gowran
runners_data.spotlight: Earned a modest mark on the Flat; promising to do better over hurdles as he bumped into useful opposition before winning his maiden on heavy ground at Gowran when tongue tied for the first time; this demands plenty more, however.

races.paceDynamic: Kai Lung, Proactif, Moulin Labbe and Harwa will ensure a genuine gallop from the start, with four confirmed front-runners in a 10-horse field creating inevitable pressure up front. The soft ground will compound stamina demands as these pace-setters drag each other along, likely creating a searching test. With four runners also wanting prominent positions (Macho Man, Majolique, Adrienne, Michonne), traffic problems are guaranteed turning for home. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses like North Shore and Minella Boss who can benefit from the pace collapse and find clear running late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Closers
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners (Kai Lung, Proactif, Moulin Labbe, Harwa) go too fast early on soft ground
scenarios.body: The leaders will weaken from 2 out, allowing hold-up horses with clear runs to sweep past tired rivals. North Shore's class and Minella Boss's finishing kick become decisive advantages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Mullins Front-Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of Proactif or Kai Lung can dictate fractions and control the pace
scenarios.body: Willie Mullins' superior tactical awareness allows his front-runner to time their effort perfectly, staying clear of the traffic behind. The winner comes from having both the pace control and the class to sustain their effort.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Runner Times Move
scenarios.trigger: If the midfield congestion allows a prominent runner to find the perfect split 2 out
scenarios.body: Macho Man or Majolique can avoid the pace battle while staying close enough to strike when gaps appear. Their tactical positioning proves superior to both the struggling leaders and traffic-hit hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Benefits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle and traffic problems eliminate all the fancied runners
scenarios.body: Adrienne or Michonne find themselves in the right place when carnage unfolds ahead, inheriting victory through superior positioning. The soft ground aids their stamina while others have expended too much energy.

watchPoints.text: Watch for early pace battle between Kai Lung, Proactif, Moulin Labbe and Harwa burning each other out before halfway
Monitor North Shore's early position as he needs to settle and conserve energy for his trademark late surge
Check if Macho Man can secure ideal prominent pitch without getting caught in the midfield squeeze
Observe Minella Boss's jumping rhythm early as the tongue-tie addition suggests temperament concerns
Watch for any market moves on the Mullins runners as stable has strong 14-day form and multiple chances

runners_data.name: Eclipse Chaser
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer with tongue-tie for Mullins, 63 days off after mixed recent form pattern

runners_data.name: Grann's Boy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner returning after 163 days, course winner last year who holds form well after breaks
runners_data.comment: Won on this card last year, fit from recent run on the Flat, interesting runner

runners_data.name: Kovanis

races.paceDynamic: Eagles Reign is the sole confirmed front-runner and will get an uncontested lead, allowing him to set a measured tempo early before potentially quickening. The prominent runners like Meet And Greet, Timeless Treaty, Fierce Handay and Hgranca De Thaix will track behind but none are aggressive pace pressers. This creates a tactical race where the pace will be reasonable early but not searching, before a long sustained drive from the home turn. The sustainable gallop and long run-in clearly favours horses with tactical speed and finishing kick - hold-up horses will get the perfect setup to unleash late runs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Eagles Reign sets his usual measured tempo without early pressure...
scenarios.body: The pace will be moderate early allowing closers to position perfectly before unleashing finishing kicks up the long Fairyhouse straight. Welonlyhavedone, Shabby Hill, Jony R and Fiveonefive all have the tactical speed to pick up leaders in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group decides to apply more pressure from halfway...
scenarios.body: This forces Eagles Reign into a more searching gallop, setting up the race for horses tracking in behind with natural cruising speed. Timeless Treaty and Fierce Handay are perfectly positioned to capitalize while Meet And Greet could find renewed form.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Eagles Reign gets his fractions perfect and kicks clear turning in...
scenarios.body: The uncontested leader could prove hard to peg back if he times his effort right, especially with the step back up in trip suiting. Healys Pub could emerge from the pack as the main danger given his recent Naas success.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop becomes pedestrian with no one willing to commit...
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish where horses with the most natural pace over shorter trips gain an advantage. Blue Mosque and Arch Empire could benefit from their 2m speed in a slowly-run contest.

watchPoints.text: Eagles Reign could steal this if allowed uncontested fractions - watch for any early pressure from the prominent group
Must Go Now has shown a pattern of fading in the finish when the pace lifts in the final furlong
Meet And Greet wears first-time cheekpieces after a 78-day break which could spark improvement or hint at problems
Several runners return from long breaks including Slane Hill (240 days) and Grann's Boy (163 days) who may need the run
The prominent group including Timeless Treaty and Fierce Handay could unite to pressure Eagles Reign if they choose to be aggressive

runners_data.name: Brewin'upastorm

runners_data.name: Kawaboomga
runners_data.note: Only true leader will control tempo but 51 days off and needs to prove stamina at this trip
runners_data.comment: Eyecatching novice form; should be all the sharper for his belated return at Gowran
runners_data.spotlight: Smart novice who wasn't beaten far by Kopek Des Bordes in a maiden before beating the smart William Munny next time out (on soft); finished behind Storm Heart and Farren Glory in the Grade 3 Red Mills at Gowran (heavy) but ran well after a long absence and he should be considerably sharper here; 3lb better off with Storm Heart.

runners_data.name: The Yellow Clay
runners_data.note: Prominent runner carrying 9lbs penalty whose recent form shows concerning falls and poor efforts
runners_data.comment: Classy novice; going okay when departing three out in a handicap at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: High class novice last season who was second to The New Lion in the 2m5f Grade 1 at Cheltenham; later suffered a heavy fall at Punchestown; this campaign hasn't really got off the ground and departed too far out (three from home) in the 2m5f handicap at the Festival (Storm Heart third) to know how he would have fared, though was going well enough at the time; wouldn't be a surprise to see him get his career back on track.

runners_data.name: Bowensonfire
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to avoid early congestion and sweep late off strong recent form
runners_data.comment: Admirably consistent handicapper; Jack Kennedy prefers the chances of The Yellow Clay
runners_data.spotlight: Admirably consistent handicapper who didn't run too badly when midfield in the County Hurdle last month; however, this is a step up the ladder for him and regular rider Jack Kennedy evidently prefers the chances of The Yellow Clay.

runners_data.name: Blizzard Of Oz
runners_data.note: Prominent runner but Paul Townend's defection to Storm Heart speaks volumes about chances
runners_data.comment: Still below his best when winning at Thurles; Paul Townend deserts him for Storm Heart
runners_data.spotlight: Got his career back on track on returning to hurdles at Thurles (2m7f, soft to heavy), but that was still beneath his peak form and Paul Townend deserts him for Storm Heart.

runners_data.name: Glen Kiln
runners_data.note: Prominent type with good recent Grade 1 form but 71 days absence is significant concern
runners_data.comment: Appreciated the drop in grade when making all in a Grade 3 at Naas; commands respect
runners_data.spotlight: Better than ever this season and has contested two Grade 1s; appreciated the drop in class when making all in a Grade 3 at Naas (2m, heavy) and this 7yo is a good bet to give his running (stays this far); very sound jumper.

runners_data.name: Grainne A Chroi
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner stepping up markedly in class but won last time and suits tactical scenario
runners_data.comment: This is more demanding against male opposition and has her work cut out at the weights
runners_data.spotlight: Doubled her tally under rules when emerging from off the pace to narrowly win the Grade 3 Quevega at Punchestown (2m4f, soft); this is appreciably more demanding against male opposition and has her work cut out at the weights.

runners_data.name: Farren Glory
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who hasn't won for over a year and beaten by several of these already this season
runners_data.comment: Held by some of these and last time he was pulled up in a handicap at Cheltenham
runners_data.spotlight: Grade 1-winning novice and won over fences last season; hasn't really reached the heights he once promised and was beaten in races won by Glen Kiln and Storm Heart before pulling up in the 2m5f handicap at Cheltenham when tried in cheekpieces (retained).

races.paceDynamic: Kawaboomga is the only genuine front-runner and will dictate a sustainable early tempo without pressure. Storm Heart, Slade Steel, Brewin'upastorm, The Yellow Clay, and Blizzard Of Oz will create serious congestion in the prominent positions, with four or five wanting to track closely. This congestion will create traffic problems from the third-last hurdle as horses begin to make their moves. The clean early pace followed by late tactical complications strongly favours hold-up horses who can avoid the scrimmaging and produce late runs when others are stopping after battling for position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-up horses prosper
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pack gets tangled up from 3 out as expected
scenarios.body: Bowensonfire and Grainne A Chroi will have clear runs while the prominent brigade compromise each other. Their patient tactics prove decisive as they sweep past tired leaders who've been fighting for position throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-runner stays clear
scenarios.trigger: If Kawaboomga gets an uncontested lead and the chasers mark each other
scenarios.body: The 6-year-old maintains his advantage as the prominent horses neutralise each other's chances through over-racing. His sustainable galloping style proves perfect for the testing conditions and trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent positioning wins
scenarios.trigger: If one prominent horse avoids the traffic and gets first run
scenarios.body: Storm Heart or The Yellow Clay times their move perfectly before the congestion develops. Their class tells as they kick clear while others are still organising their challenges from behind.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace collapses completely
scenarios.trigger: If Kawaboomga goes too slow and no one pressures early
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last hurdle with superior class prevailing regardless of tactics. The highest-rated horses prevail in a bunched finish despite tactical positioning.

watchPoints.text: Watch for traffic problems from 3 out when Storm Heart, Slade Steel, The Yellow Clay and Blizzard Of Oz all need racing room simultaneously
Monitor Kawaboomga's stamina as he's never won beyond 2m and may tire if pace quickens dramatically
Check if Bowensonfire gets the patient ride his hold-up style demands rather than being committed too early
Observe The Yellow Clay's jumping under pressure given his recent falls and whether the 9lb penalty hampers his effort
Watch Glen Kiln's fitness after 71-day break particularly in the closing stages of this competitive heat

races.name: Underwriting Exchange Fairyhouse Chase (Grade 2)

runners_data.name: Energumene
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven class but age concerns at 12, though Paul Townend's tactical awareness could prove crucial in getting the timing right
runners_data.comment: Top class in pomp but time catching up with him, held by Found A Fifty on Cork run in Dec'

runners_data.name: Blood Destiny
runners_data.note: Natural leader who bounced back from a poor run with Grade 3 win last time, Brian Hayes will need to judge pace carefully to avoid over-racing

runners_data.name: Saint Sam
runners_data.note: Aggressive front-runner who was narrowly beaten in this race last year, proven course form gives him tactical edge but needs to avoid going too fast early
runners_data.comment: Runner up in this last year behind Found A Fifty, needs to leave last two efforts behind
runners_data.spotlight: Six-time chase winner but no success since a Grade 2 win at Clonmel in November 2024; ran a cracker in this last year to finish a 0.75l second behind Found A Fifty; below par in both runs this season and needs to leave those tame efforts behind.

runners_data.name: Found A Fifty

runners_data.comment: Beat Energumene at Cork in Dec', won this last year, pulled up latest but the one to beat

runners_data.spotlight: 2-6 over fences; won the Navan Listed handicap in 2024, that Down Memory Lane won last year, off 143, which was his last success; excellent effort in the Grade 2 Red Mills at Gowran in February when a 1.25l second behind Impaire Et Passe; well beaten in the Martin Pipe latest but the return to chasing is a plus; a fair bit to find on the figures, however.

runners_data.name: Down Memory Lane
runners_data.note: Back-marker who won well at Navan in December, Mark Walsh will need significant pace collapse to bring his closing kick into play
runners_data.comment: Both chase wins at Navan, disappointed at Cheltenham latest, could bounce back
runners_data.spotlight: Won his bumper here; both chase wins have come at Navan; won a 20.5f Listed handicap chase on testing ground there off 144 in December; disappointed when third-favourite for the Plate Handicap at Cheltenham; better than that and has a good chance at the weights; can't be discounted.

races.paceDynamic: Saint Sam and Blood Destiny will contest the early pace as two natural front-runners, with Saint Sam likely to press or share the lead given his aggressive style. The soft ground and 2m4f trip suggests they'll set a solid but not breakneck gallop, allowing the field to stay reasonably compact through the early stages. Found A Fifty and Energumene will track prominently behind the leaders, while the hold-up pair Sa Fureur and Down Memory Lane will be positioned towards the rear. This shape strongly favours prominent runners who can position close to the pace and avoid getting trapped behind a wall of horses when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not excessive, allowing prominent trackers to stay within striking distance
scenarios.body: Found A Fifty and Energumene can use their class and tactical speed to pick off the front-runners in the straight. The soft ground and testing finish will expose any lack of stamina from horses coming from too far back.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If one of the leaders can dictate terms and steal crucial lengths at the business end
scenarios.body: Saint Sam or Blood Destiny could capitalize on their natural pace advantage and make it a test of stamina from the front. The winner would need to respond to challenges while maintaining galloping room on the testing surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Charges
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong and the leaders come back dramatically in the final half-mile
scenarios.body: Sa Fureur or Down Memory Lane could benefit from a strong pace collapse, using their closing kick to sweep past tired leaders. The soft going would aid their late charge but they need significant pace bias to overcome class deficit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners go too fast early and the race becomes a lottery in testing conditions
scenarios.body: The entire field could come together in a messy finish where stamina and jumping accuracy matter most. Any horse still traveling well with two to jump could capitalize on a pace-collapsed race.

watchPoints.text: Saint Sam and Blood Destiny could go too fast early if they get into a speed duel, which would set up the race for prominent trackers
Energumene needs to be traveling strongly with three to jump as his stamina reserves may not be what they once were at age 12
Down Memory Lane requires a strong pace and may struggle to get into contention if the leaders are allowed to dictate soft fractions
Found A Fifty must avoid getting shuffled back if the pace is slow, as his prominent style depends on maintaining position throughout
The soft ground could level the playing field if it becomes testing enough to expose any fitness or stamina concerns in the older horses

races.paceDynamic: Kiss Will, Soldier In Milan, and O'Toole will ensure a strong gallop from the start in this 30-runner marathon, with The Jukebox Kid, Better Days Ahead, and Kurasso Blue also prominent early. The fierce pace combined with testing ground conditions will see stamina become the decisive factor from the home turn onwards. With 12 runners wanting prominent positions, expect significant traffic problems approaching the business end. This punishing pace scenario strongly favours hold-up horses with proven stamina reserves who can pick off tired leaders late.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Strong Gallop Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Kiss Will and Soldier In Milan maintain a fierce gallop to halfway on this testing ground
scenarios.body: The relentless pace will see multiple prominent runners tire dramatically from three out, opening the door for patient hold-up performers with superior stamina reserves. Fresh finishers will sweep past exhausted pace-setters in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tactical Prominent Success
scenarios.trigger: If the early leaders settle into a more measured rhythm after the initial burst
scenarios.body: Better positioned prominent runners can conserve energy for a sustained drive, with their forward position proving crucial when the pace intensifies from the home turn. Those tracking the pace without being caught up front benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field creates significant interference in the straight as tired horses fall back
scenarios.body: Several hold-up horses will find their runs blocked by weakening runners, allowing those with cleaner passages or already better positioned to capitalize. Mid-division runners with stamina prove best placed to avoid the carnage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Survival
scenarios.trigger: If the testing conditions fail to stop one of the main pace-setters completely
scenarios.body: A brave front runner maintains enough reserves to repel late challenges, benefiting from the perfect combination of stamina and tactical position. The strong early gallop actually sets up their staying power advantage.

races.paceDynamic: Prophet's Corner is the only confirmed front-runner and will dictate terms without serious pressure through the early stages. With most rivals adopting prominent or hold-up tactics, the pace will likely be steady rather than searching over this staying trip on testing ground. The lack of pace pressure means the gallop may not be strong enough to set up the race for closers, while Prophet's Corner gets an uncontested lead to utilize. This race shape strongly favours front-runners and prominent racers who can track the leader and strike turning for home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Prophet's Corner gets an easy lead and isn't headed until late
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace allows Prophet's Corner to dictate ideal fractions and kick clear when challenged, while prominent trackers get first run but can't peg back the leader. Prophet's Corner benefits from the tactical advantage while strong stayers like Butch Cassidy and Barry Lyndon get competitive positions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the prominent racers travels strongly and times their challenge perfectly
scenarios.body: The steady early gallop suits the prominent brigade who can sit close without expending energy, then quicken past a tiring Prophet's Corner in the final half-mile. Butch Cassidy or Ayiko use their class edge to overhaul the leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses completely and becomes a sprint from the last mile
scenarios.body: The lack of early gallop creates a tactical affair where stamina becomes less important than a strong finish, allowing hold-up horses to close late. Savante or Cave Court benefit from the lack of early pace and finish strongest.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Chaos Benefits Outsider
scenarios.trigger: If Prophet's Corner stops quickly and prominent horses get caught in traffic
scenarios.body: Early leader fades badly turning for home while the fancied prominent horses get shuffled back or hampered, creating opportunities for lightly-weighted runners. Well Del or Ney capitalize on the pace collapse with their lower weights.

races.paceDynamic: Jeroboam Machin, Charismatic Kid, Soul Asylum and Poetisa will ensure a fierce early gallop over this 2m trip on soft ground. The quartet of confirmed front-runners guarantees a strong pace from flag to finish, with no respite as they battle for control. This sustained tempo will stretch the field and expose stamina limitations on the testing ground conditions. The relentless pace strongly favours prominent racers who can track the leaders without expending excess energy, while hold-up horses face an uphill task getting into contention from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Gallop Grind
scenarios.trigger: If the four front-runners maintain a fierce tempo throughout
scenarios.body: The strong pace will suit prominent trackers who can position close enough to strike without leading. State Pension and Luidgi Du Luy are perfectly positioned to capitalise when the pace-setters tire.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Dominates Field
scenarios.trigger: If Jeroboam Machin or Charismatic Kid controls the tempo
scenarios.body: One of the class leaders dictates more measured fractions and kicks clear with superior ability. The Grade 2 winner's class or Elliott's shrewd handling proves decisive in the finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mullins Tactical Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Poetisa is held up despite her leading tendencies
scenarios.body: Patrick Mullins employs patient tactics, allowing the front-runners to burn each other out before unleashing a finishing kick. Her Cheltenham form and tactical versatility gives her a unique edge late on.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Shock Success
scenarios.trigger: If the market leaders falter on testing ground conditions
scenarios.body: The soft ground or fierce pace finds out the favourites' stamina or ground handling. Leonard Vallis's proven soft ground form or a well-backed point winner springs a surprise.
